provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.

provenance.original: Based on past estimates, TSA estimates that it will receive approximately 9,000 claims on an annual basis, or 750 per month.  Currently, all claims are submitted manually.  TSA estimates that it will take 30 minutes to complete and submit the forms, which results in an estimated burden of 4,500 hours.  Additionally, TSA collects payment information from those members of the public whose claims are approved by TSA.  TSA estimates that approximately 1,250 claims are approved each year.  TSA estimates it takes ten minutes (0.1667 hours) to submit payment information for an annual hour burden of 208 hours.  TSA estimates the public average annual hour burden of 4,708 hours (4,500 + 208).  To estimate annual hour burden cost, TSA multiples each hour burden by a fully-loaded wage rate of $38.91.  TSA estimates an annual hour burden cost of $175,095 for filing a claim and $8,106 for submitting payment information, for a total annual hour burden cost of this collection of $183,201.  Therefore, the total 3-year hour burden cost of this collection is $549,604 ($183,201 x 3 = $549,604).
provenance.transformation: Minutes retained; hours ×60 where necessary; separate additive tasks and respondent roles

provenance.original: Based on past estimates, TSA estimates that it will receive approximately 7,500 claims on an annual basis.  Currently, all claims are submitted in writing by mail.  TSA estimates that it will take 30 minutes (0.5 hours) to complete and submit the forms, which results in an estimated burden of 3,750 hours.  Additionally, TSA collects payment information from those members of the public whose claims are approved by TSA.  TSA estimates that approximately 900 claims are approved each year.  TSA estimates it takes 10 minutes (0.1667 hours) to submit payment information for an annual hour burden of 150 hours.  TSA estimates that of the 900 claims approved each year, TSA will ask only two claimants per year to complete TSA Form 600.  TSA estimates the time to complete TSA Form 600 is 2.5 minutes.  As the usage of the form is rare, TSA estimates the burden to be de minimis.

provenance.original: TSA TPO handles the submitted information in the same manner for responses from MSIJSOC and TPO programs covered by this collection.  TSA estimates that each response requires 15 minutes (0.25 hours) to process, submit and file by TSA F or G band employees.  TSA uses a fully loaded average hourly wage rate of $56.98 for these employees.  TSA estimates the hour burden cost for TSA (or Federal Government) by multiplying the number of responses by the time it takes to process each response and the fully loaded average hourly wage rate of employees processing, submitting, and filing the responses.  TSA estimates that the total hour burden cost is $76,018 for TSA to process, submit and file the information received.
